steps.title: Assemble perfusion switching apparatus
steps.instruction: Cut two 30 cm pieces of Tygon 3/32 in tubing (Tygon E‑3603). Screw a Luer‑lock female connector onto each end, attach the tubing, then connect a 25 G scalp‑vein butterfly set to the male Luer‑lock. Verify all connections are secure.

steps.title: Prepare perfusion syringes
steps.instruction: Fill two 60 mL syringes: one with ice‑cold, oxygenated ACSF containing 10 U mL⁻¹ heparin (prepare fresh, keep on ice, oxygenate 30 min–1 h), the other with the chosen fixative (either 4 % (w/v) PFA or 9 % (v/v) glyoxal + 8 % (v/v) acetic acid, pH 4, chilled on ice, prepare fresh).

steps.title: Prime tubing with fixative then ACSF
steps.instruction: Attach the fixative syringe to the tubing designated for fixative, push the plunger to flush fixative through the tubing and butterfly set. Then repeat with the ACSF syringe to flush out residual fixative, leaving the line filled with ACSF.

steps.title: Set up dissection workspace
steps.instruction: Place a vinyl dissecting pad in the center of the bench, arrange all dissection tools (scissors, forceps, hemostat, micro‑spoon, etc.) as shown in Figure 1B, and prepare anesthesia supplies (isoflurane‑infused cotton balls, ketamine/xylazine vials) in the fume hood.

steps.title: Induce anesthesia with isoflurane
steps.instruction: Place the mouse in a large beaker covered with aluminum foil, insert cotton balls soaked in isoflurane, and expose the animal until it cannot right itself (≈30 s).

steps.title: Maintain anesthesia
steps.instruction: Inject intraperitoneally ketamine 100 mg kg⁻¹ and xylazine 10 mg kg⁻¹ (alternative: 4 % isoflurane in O₂ via a VetFlo system).

steps.title: Secure mouse on vinyl pad
steps.instruction: Insert two 21 G × 1 in needles through the skin at the axilla and inguinal regions to immobilize all four limbs on the vinyl pad.

steps.title: Disinfect abdomen
steps.instruction: Apply 70 % (v/v) ethanol to the abdominal skin.

steps.title: Open abdominal cavity
steps.instruction: Cut skin and underlying muscle along the midline from the snout to the xiphoid process, then laterally along the lower ribs using straight operating scissors (#5).

steps.title: Expose chest cavity
steps.instruction: Cut the diaphragm perimeter to reveal the thoracic cavity, then cut away ribs on both sides to expose the pericardial cavity, taking care not to nick the heart.

steps.title: Insert perfusion needle
steps.instruction: Pinch the left ventricular apex with a hemostat, insert the 25 G butterfly needle (connected to the ACSF line) into the ventricle, and lock the needle in place with the hemostat.

steps.title: Create outflow
steps.instruction: Cut through the right atrium with clean straight dissecting scissors (#7) to allow blood to exit.

steps.title: Perfuse with heparinized ACSF
steps.instruction: Run ice‑cold, heparin‑containing ACSF at 7 mL min⁻¹ for ~2 min (≈14 mL). Blood should clear, liver lighten, lungs turn white.

steps.title: Perfuse with fixative
steps.instruction: Switch flow to the fixative (4 % PFA or 9 % glyoxal + 8 % acetic acid, pH 4) and perfuse ~60 mL at the same 7 mL min⁻¹ rate. Muscles and tail will contract, indicating fixation. Avoid bubbles when switching.

steps.title: Decapitate and expose brain
steps.instruction: Decapitate with straight operating scissors, make a sagittal scalp incision from snout to back, remove the skull with dissecting scissors and forceps, and gently lift the brain with a micro‑spoon, severing cranial nerves.

steps.title: Post‑fix brain overnight
steps.instruction: Place the brain in a 15 mL conical tube containing 10–14 mL of the same fixative used for perfusion. Incubate at 4 °C overnight.

steps.title: Wash brain in PBS
steps.instruction: Replace fixative with 10 mL 1× PBS, incubate 5–10 min at room temperature (RT) with gentle agitation. Repeat two more times for a total of three washes.

steps.title: Pause point – short‑term storage
steps.instruction: After the final PBS wash, brains may be stored in 1× PBS at 4 °C for up to one week.

steps.title: Cryoprotect brain – 15 % sucrose
steps.instruction: Immerse the brain in 15 % (w/v) sucrose in 0.1 M phosphate buffer (PB) and incubate overnight at 4 °C until the brain sinks.

steps.title: Cryoprotect brain – 30 % sucrose
steps.instruction: Transfer the brain to 30 % (w/v) sucrose in 0.1 M PB and incubate at 4 °C until it sinks again (typically several days).

steps.title: Prepare dry‑ice/2‑methylbutane bath
steps.instruction: Fill a 100 mL stainless steel beaker placed in a dry‑ice‑filled ice bucket with 50–60 mL 2‑methylbutane. Allow the bath to reach –70 °C to –80 °C (verify with a thermometer).

steps.title: Fill embedding molds with OCT
steps.instruction: Place 12 mm × 12 mm × 20 mm embedding molds halfway full of OCT compound.

steps.title: Mount brain in OCT
steps.instruction: Remove the brain from the sucrose solution, blot excess liquid on a Kimwipe, place the brain (olfactory bulbs down) into the half‑filled mold, then fill the remainder of the mold with OCT. Avoid bubbles.

steps.title: Freeze embedded brain
steps.instruction: Using long forceps, hold the mold in the 2‑methylbutane bath (do not submerge; keep the mold above the liquid) until the OCT solidifies (2–3 min). Wrap the mold in aluminum foil and store at –80 °C.

steps.title: Pause point – long‑term storage
steps.instruction: Embedded brains can be kept at –80 °C for years.

steps.title: Prepare gelatin and chromium solutions
steps.instruction: Make gelatin solution (5 mg mL⁻¹) by dissolving 4.5 g gelatin in 900 mL Milli‑Q water on a heated stir plate. Make 1 mM chromium potassium sulfate solution by dissolving 450 mg in 30 mL Milli‑Q water. Both solutions are prepared fresh and used immediately.

steps.title: Sonicate coverslips in ethanol
steps.instruction: Place #1.5 rectangular coverslips (both sides exposed) in a plastic staining rack, submerge the rack in 95 % (v/v) ethanol in a 2 L beaker, and sonicate for 15 min.

steps.title: Air‑dry coverslips
steps.instruction: Remove coverslips, place on paper towels, and let air‑dry.

steps.title: Mix gelatin and chromium solutions
steps.instruction: Combine gelatin and chromium potassium sulfate solutions 1:1 (equal volumes).

steps.title: Sub coverslips
steps.instruction: Immerse the dried coverslips in the 1:1 gelatin‑chromium mixture, swirl gently for 1 min, then wick excess liquid with a Kimwipe. Allow coverslips to dry at RT overnight. Store dried, subbed coverslips in their original boxes at RT.

steps.title: Equilibrate embedded brain for cryosectioning
steps.instruction: Transfer the frozen block from –80 °C to a –20 °C freezer and keep for 12 h before sectioning.

steps.title: Set cryostat temperatures
steps.instruction: Set object temperature (OT) to –21 °C and chamber temperature (CT) to –25 °C.

steps.title: Install and cool cryostat blade
steps.instruction: Insert a low‑profile microtome blade into the knife holder, secure it, and allow it to cool for at least 15 min.

steps.title: Mount brain on specimen disc
steps.instruction: Cut open the OCT mold with a razor blade, place the brain onto a specimen disc that has a thin layer of OCT on its base, let the OCT freeze to secure the tissue, then lock the disc onto the specimen head.

steps.title: Trim to region of interest
steps.instruction: Advance the specimen head until tissue is just in front of the blade, set trimming thickness to 30 µm, and trim using the mouse brain atlas until reaching ~‑1.05 mm posterior to bregma for somatosensory cortex (S1). Adjust head angle and anti‑roll plate to keep sections flat.

steps.title: Collect 6 µm sections
steps.instruction: Set section thickness to 6 µm and collect sections onto gelatin‑coated #1.5 coverslips (prepared in step D). Verify under a transmitted‑light microscope that sections are free of tears, bubbles, or folds.

steps.title: Pause point – section storage
steps.instruction: Dry sections can be stored at –80 °C in sealed slide boxes for several months.

steps.title: Set up humidified staining system
steps.instruction: Partially fill the bottom reservoir of a Simport Scientific Slide Staining System with distilled water and place it on a flat surface.

steps.title: Block tissue
steps.instruction: Place a CoverWell chamber (300 µL capacity) gasket side up into the humidified system, add 300 µL blocking buffer (1× PBS, 5 % normal goat serum, 0.5 % Triton X‑100), lay the tissue‑side‑down coverslip onto the buffer, ensure even spreading and no bubbles, then cover the system and incubate at 4 °C overnight.

steps.title: Prepare primary antibody solution
steps.instruction: Dilute primary antibodies or nanobodies in blocking buffer to the concentrations listed in Table S1.

steps.title: Incubate with primary antibodies
steps.instruction: Place fresh CoverWell chambers into the staining system, add 300 µL of the primary solution to each, transfer the coverslips (remove excess buffer with Kimwipes), and incubate at 4 °C for 48 h (up to 72 h).

steps.title: Wash after primary incubation
steps.instruction: Fill Coplin jars with 1× PBS, submerge coverslips, and incubate 5 min at RT. Repeat two more times for a total of three 5‑min washes (no agitation).

steps.title: Incubate with secondary antibodies
steps.instruction: Add 300 µL of secondary antibodies (diluted in blocking buffer) to new CoverWell chambers, place coverslips, and incubate 2–3 h at RT.

steps.title: Wash after secondary incubation
steps.instruction: Perform three 5‑min washes in 1× PBS as above, then a single 5‑min wash in 0.1 M phosphate buffer (PB).

steps.title: Brief air‑dry tissue
steps.instruction: Remove coverslips from the PB wash and air‑dry the tissue for 1–2 min (do not let it dry completely).

steps.title: Mount coverslip on slide
steps.instruction: Place 200 µL ProLong Glass antifade mountant onto a labeled microscope slide, gently lower the coverslip (tissue side down) starting at the long edge to avoid bubbles, and let the mountant spread evenly.

steps.title: Cure mounting medium
steps.instruction: Allow the slide to cure in a dry, dark area at RT for at least 48 h. For long‑term storage, seal the coverslip edges with nail polish and keep slides at 4 °C in the dark.

steps.title: Align STED lasers
steps.instruction: Using 80 nm gold particles, align each STED laser (CW 592 nm, CW 660 nm, pulsed 775 nm) so that the excitation beam passes through the center of the STED donut (offset < 25 nm). Wear appropriate PPE for laser work.

steps.title: Configure imaging sequence
Set imaging parameters
steps.instruction: Use a 100× 1.4 NA objective, 1,024 × 1,024 pixel format, digital zoom ≈ 4.5. Set pixel size to ~20 nm when using the pulsed 775 nm STED (or 40 nm for CW‑only). Acquire Z‑stacks at 150–180 nm intervals. Allocate 20 % of each STED laser power to the Z‑donut for 3D STED.

steps.title: Calibrate resolution with nanorulers
steps.instruction: Image GATTA nanorulers (50, 70, 140 nm spacing) in each channel to verify lateral resolution (~50 nm for pulsed 775 nm, ≥ 80 nm for CW) and adjust STED power accordingly. Use 3D GATTA bead spacers to set Z‑resolution.

steps.title: Configure FLIM‑tau STED (optional)
steps.instruction: Set HyD‑X detectors to photon‑counting mode, aim for 5–10 photons pixel⁻¹. Adjust “tau strength” in the FALCON module to 100–150 for images with ~10 photons pixel⁻¹. If FALCON is unavailable, set detectors to ignore photons < 1–3 ns after the laser pulse.

steps.title: Process images in Fiji
steps.instruction: Subtract background by removing the mean intensity of the whole 1,024 × 1,024 frame from each channel, adjust brightness to the maximum gray value per Z‑stack, convert 16‑bit images to 8‑bit, and apply a Gaussian blur of 0.5–0.8 pixels to each STED channel.

steps.title: Analyze data
steps.instruction: Perform quantitative analyses (cluster size, number, intensity) using software such as Imaris or Neurolucida 360. For 3D STED Z‑stacks, reconstruct 3D volumes to verify synaptic localization.
